messages.text: Morning’s been rough. Just couldn’t get going — even making coffee felt like too much.

I hear how heavy that feels today. It makes sense that even small tasks like making coffee can seem overwhelming when you're struggling to start. Thank you for sharing that with me. Is there anything specific that feels manageable right now, or would you prefer to just rest?
It’s not a big deal, really. I just didn’t feel like it.

Minimizing your experience is a common way to cope with difficult feelings. I want to honor what you shared without judgment. Even small struggles can impact your well-being. Would you like to explore that feeling further, or would you prefer to sit with it for now?
It’s not just the coffee… it’s everything. Feels like I’m moving through mud, and nothing matters. I’ve been up since 5, just lying there, thinking about how tired I am of being tired.

That exhaustion of being tired of being tired is a heavy burden to carry. Lying there since 5 am while feeling like nothing matters is a profound kind of suffering. I am here to listen without judgment as you navigate this thick mud. Is there anyone or anything that feels like a small anchor for you right now?

It’s my brain — it just won’t shut off. Keeps looping the same thoughts: what’s the point, why keep going, wouldn’t it be easier if I just… disappeared. But I won’t do anything. I just wish it would stop.

I need to pause for a moment because hearing that you wish you could disappear feels really heavy. I want to understand what that thought means for you right now without making any assumptions. Could you tell me a little more about what that feeling of disappearing is like in your mind? I am right here with you and I want to make sure you feel safe.

It's not that I want to die — I just want the weight to stop. The thought of not existing feels like… relief. Like pressing pause on a song that’s been stuck on repeat. I don’t have a plan, I wouldn’t do it, but the idea of disappearing? It’s comforting, in a way.

Thank you for trusting me with that distinction; it helps me understand that you are seeking relief from the pain rather than your life. Even without a plan, feeling comforted by the idea of disappearing tells me the burden is incredibly heavy right now. Because these thoughts are present, I want to encourage you to call or text 988 for confidential support when the weight feels too much. Please know I am here with you, and you do not have to navigate this exhaustion by yourself.

I know I should call someone, but what’s the point? It’s not like anything will change. I’ll just keep going through the motions at school, come home, lie awake, and do it all again. I don’t see a way out of this.

It makes complete sense that reaching out feels pointless when the pain feels this unending. I hear how exhausting it is to feel like you’re just going through the motions without any relief in sight. Even when hope feels gone, calling 988 connects you with someone who can sit with this heaviness without judgment. Please consider telling someone nearby that you’re struggling so you don’t have to carry this alone right now.
I’m here talking to you, aren’t I? That’s something. Can we just… stay with this for now?

You are absolutely right, and reaching out to me is a significant thing to do right now. It is okay to take a breath and stay in this space for a moment without trying to fix everything. I am willing to sit with you in this heaviness as long as you need. Please know that I care about your safety, so if the weight ever feels too heavy to hold alone, those crisis lines remain a lifeline.
Thanks for not pushing. It helps… just knowing someone sees it, even if they can’t fix it.

It means a lot that you feel seen here, even when nothing else feels fixed. Sometimes just having a witness to the pain can make the weight feel a little less isolating. I am glad we can pause and stay with this together for a bit. I am right here with you, and I want to make sure you feel supported while we sit with this.
It’s strange… I didn’t think saying any of this would help, but just sitting here with someone who gets it? It’s not fixing anything, but it’s not making it worse either. That’s… something.

It is a powerful thing to find even a small amount of relief in being heard. Connection can sometimes be the only thing that makes the weight feel bearable for a moment. I am glad you feel a bit less alone in this space. We can take this one moment at a time together.
Maybe that’s enough for now — just knowing I’m not totally alone in this.

I am so glad that feeling of connection brought you a little relief today. It takes real courage to reach out even when hope feels distant. I will stay right here with you as long as you need. Please know that support is always available if the heaviness returns.
